newsitem.title: USA: Envirodyne files lawsuit vs largest holder.
newsitem.headline: Envirodyne files lawsuit vs largest holder.

text.p: Envirodyne Industries Inc on Thursday said it filed a lawsuit in a federal court in Chicago against its largest stockholder, Zapata Corp, and several of Zapata's principals.

The suit alleges they misled Envirodyne shareholders about their intentions regarding control of Envirodyne. It claims Zapata, which owns a 40.1-percent stake in Envirodyne, and the principals violated federal securities laws by filing false and misleading statements with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Envirodyne said Zapata Chairman Malcolm Glazer recently told stockholders he was not demanding control of the company, but Zapata has admitted in regulatory filings it is attempting to gain control.
Zapata officials were not immediately available to comment on the Envirodyne lawsuit.

Last week, Zapata said it filed preliminary proxy materials against Envirodyne's current seven-member board and said it would nominate Glazer, his son Avram and Robert Leffler for election to a revamped five-member board.
Envirodyne has said it vigorously opposes the Glazer slate of nominees.

Malcolm Glazer and his son are already on Envirodyne's board but were not slated for reelection earlier this month after Malcolm Glazer refused to agree not to seek control of the company for the next 12 months.
Envirodyne makes food packaging and food supplies.
